newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end with technical gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end with technical gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Tuesday in moderate trade, driven by a steady wave of short covering and technical buying when prices held support early in the session, sources said.
December climbed 10.1 cents to close at $2.674 per million British thermal units. January settled 9.3 cents higher at $2.65. Other deferreds ended up by one-half to 7.5 cents.

"We bounced off the uptrend line, and technicals could move us a little higher, but I think we'll need some real cold to get back over $2.80 (basis December)," said one Houston-based trader, noting cash was soft today.

Chartists said December held important trendline support early Tuesday in the $2.52-2.53 area, also a prominent low from late October. They pegged resistance at $2.72 and then at the $2.88 contract high.

While the market was oversold and due for a correction after a 10 percent slide from Friday's new contract high, traders said any paper rally would be difficult to sustain without colder weather and firmer cash numbers.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices fell almost a dime Tuesday to about the $2.60 level, about 10 cents below November indices. Midwest prices were down the same amount to the mid-to-high $2.40s, also 10 cents under Nov 1 levels. Mild weather undermined New York city gate prices, with swing down 15 cents or more to about the $2.90 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip firmed 4.4 cents to $2.177. NYMEX said five Alberta contracts traded compared with 37 on Monday.
NYMEX Permian natgas again was untraded but December ended up two cents at $2.46.

On the KCBT, December finished four cents higher at $2.513, while deferreds settled up by one half to 5.5 cents. The December East/West spread widened by 6.1 cents to 16.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 158 contracts traded, up from Monday's total of 46.
